body.title: Draft: Allow labels and annotations on Kubernetes pause pods
body.description:
<!--
This is a general Merge Request template.
Consider choosing a template from the list above if it will match your case more.
-->

## What does this MR do?

Adds two optional maps to `[runners.kubernetes.autoscaler]` that set labels and
annotations on the pause pod `Deployment`'s pod template:

```toml
[runners.kubernetes.autoscaler]
  [runners.kubernetes.autoscaler.pause_pod_labels]
    "team" = "platform-ci"
    "tags.datadoghq.com/env" = "prd"
  [runners.kubernetes.autoscaler.pause_pod_annotations]
    "example.com/arch-opt-in" = "true"
```

### Root cause

`buildDeployment` in `executors/kubernetes/autoscaler/pause_pod_manager.go` builds the pod
template with only the three runner-managed labels and no annotations. `PodSpec` fields such
as `NodeSelector`, `Tolerations`, `ServiceAccountName`, `RuntimeClassName` and
`ImagePullSecrets` are wired from configuration, but pod metadata is not.
`[runners.kubernetes] pod_labels` / `pod_annotations` are applied to job pods only, and
`KubernetesAutoscalerConfig` has no equivalent for pause pods.

Pause pods exist to hold capacity on the same nodes that job pods will use. In clusters where
scheduling or policy depends on pod metadata, pause pods without metadata end up somewhere
different from the job pods they reserve capacity for, and the feature silently does
nothing for that runner. The linked issue describes three concrete cases from a customer
running on EKS with Karpenter: a mutating webhook that rewrites `kubernetes.io/arch` unless
an opt-in annotation is present (so arm64 pause pods pinned amd64 capacity), a Kyverno
policy that flagged every pause pod as a violation, and cost attribution labels that could
be applied to every workload except the idle one.

### Why not inherit `pod_labels` / `pod_annotations`

Blind propagation would be wrong in common configurations:

- `karpenter.sh/do-not-disrupt: "true"` on job pods is correct. On pause pods it would make
  every warm node undisruptable and defeat consolidation.
- `pod-cleanup.gitlab.com/ttl` on pause pods would cause `gitlab-runner-pod-cleanup` to
  delete the warm pool on the configured interval.
- `pod_labels` values may reference job variables such as `$CI_PROJECT_ID`, which have no
  meaning for a pause pod.

The pause pod template already intentionally reuses the job pod's *scheduling* settings
(node selector, tolerations, service account, runtime class). Metadata is the exception
because the same values have opposite effects on a job and on an idle reservation.

### The fix

Follows the shape of `pause_pod_image_pull_secrets` (!6672):

1. `common/config.go`: `PausePodLabels` and `PausePodAnnotations` on `KubernetesAutoscalerConfig`.
1. `executors/kubernetes/autoscaler/provider.go`: pass both maps into `PausePodManagerConfig`.
1. `executors/kubernetes/autoscaler/pause_pod_manager.go`: merge labels into the pod template
   after the runner-managed labels. Keys in the `runner.gitlab.com` namespace, or any
   subdomain of it such as `manager.runner.gitlab.com`, are ignored with a debug log. This
   mirrors the existing rule for job pod labels in the kubernetes executor. The pattern is
   duplicated rather than shared because `executors/kubernetes` imports this package, so
   importing it back would create a cycle. The `Deployment`'s own labels and
   `Spec.Selector.MatchLabels` are unchanged, so the immutable selector cannot be broken.
   Annotations are set on the pod template only.
1. Docs: two new rows in the autoscaler settings table plus a short section on why job pod
   metadata is not inherited. Also adds the missing row for `pause_pod_image_pull_secrets`,
   which shipped in 19.1 without a docs entry.

Values are used literally. CI/CD variables are not expanded and no sanitisation is applied.

The MR is two commits so the second can be dropped independently:

1. **Feature.** Everything described above.
1. **Validation.** `createManager` and `NewPausePodManager` apply the API server's label and
   annotation rules up front using the `k8s.io/apimachinery` validation helpers this module
   already depends on (no `go.mod` change). Validation runs before any Kubernetes client or
   API call is made, because `ensureManager` retries on every `Acquire`. An invalid entry
   returns an error that names the entry and rule. `ensureManager` already handles that by
   logging a warning and not registering a manager, so jobs continue to run and only pause
   pods are skipped for that runner. Without this commit, the same misconfiguration surfaces
   as a repeating `Deployment` create error in the reconcile loop every 10 seconds. See the
   discussion comments for the full trade-off.

Changes to either map take effect on config reload. `ensureManager` already stops the old
manager, which deletes the `Deployment`, and creates a new one whenever `ConfigLoadedAt`
changes, so no new code was needed for this.

## Why was this MR needed?

Without metadata on pause pods, admission webhooks and policy engines treat them differently
from the job pods they are reserving capacity for. The only remediation available today is
to match on the `runner.gitlab.com/pause-pod=true` label in every cluster policy, which is
not possible for cost attribution and not practical when the policies are owned by another
team. The customer in the linked issue disabled pause pods (`idle_count = 0`) on the fleets
that needed them most.

## What's the best way to test this MR?

Unit tests:

```shell
go test ./common/ -run TestConfigParse -count=1
go test ./executors/kubernetes/autoscaler/ -count=1 -race
```

New tests cover TOML parsing, the merge with runner labels, reserved-namespace filtering
(including subdomain keys and mixed-case name segments), the empty case, that the
`Deployment` labels and selector never receive user metadata, that the provider wires both
maps through to the manager, that invalid keys and values are rejected by the constructor,
and that an invalid map makes `Acquire` skip manager creation without failing the job.

Manual verification against a cluster:

1. Configure a runner with the `[runners.kubernetes.autoscaler]` example above and a policy
   with `idle_count > 0`.
1. `kubectl get deploy -l runner.gitlab.com/pause-pod=true -o yaml` and confirm
   `spec.template.metadata.labels` contains the configured labels plus the three runner
   labels, `spec.template.metadata.annotations` contains the configured annotations, and
   `spec.selector.matchLabels` contains only the three runner labels.
1. Add a key such as `"runner.gitlab.com/pause-pod" = "false"` to `pause_pod_labels`, reload,
   and confirm the pause pod still carries `runner.gitlab.com/pause-pod=true` and the runner
   log (at debug level) reports the ignored key.
1. Add an invalid key such as `"team name" = "x"`, reload, and confirm the runner logs
   `Failed to start pause pod manager` naming the key, no pause pod `Deployment` exists for
   the runner, and jobs still run.
1. Remove both maps, reload, and confirm the template matches the pre-change shape.

Verification run locally: `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...` (pre-existing failures in
generated `magefiles/build/mocks.go` only), `make lint` via the pinned
`runner-linters:2.12.2-go1.26.5` image (0 issues), `go test -race ./...` (remaining
failures are host-environment only: helper arch expectations on Apple Silicon, local
timezone, `CI=0`, unix socket path length), and `vale` / `markdownlint-cli2` / `lychee` on
the changed docs page.

Pipeline note: the first pipeline on this branch passed all 84 jobs in the main pipeline.
The two failures were unrelated infrastructure: the UBI images trigger failed with
`insufficient_bridge_permissions`, and the downstream fleeting hello-world job timed out
dialing a GCP instance.

## What are the relevant issue numbers?

Closes #39844

Related: #39615 (pause pods ignore `node_affinity`, same bug class), #39395 / !6672
(`pause_pod_image_pull_secrets`, the pattern this follows).
